I take women’s rights seriously, so this is one of the first things I asked about while visiting Ghardaïa, Algeria  Now this is not necessarily for any reason. It has nothing to do with religion or location. The only thing it has to do with is that many communities that are small and follow old traditions typically give less rights and protections to women. However, I was pleasantly surprised that this is not the case in Ghardaia.   I really appreciate what I learned about  Mozabite communities, giving women in their own committees and ability to make decisions for themselves. When it comes to dress, extra protections, to feel safe and comfortable in their marriages, and the community standing in solidarity with its women. Algeria doesn’t have major fast food chains you’ll find in most countries 🇩🇿🍔 Despite being the largest country in Africa and not being under international sanctions, you still won’t find the usual McDonald’s or Burger King here. Instead, Algeria has a huge local fast food scene, with fresh and authentic ingredients in every restaurant. Instead of Five Guys here, they have Two Guys 👀 #algeria #algiers #algerianfood #streetfood #fastfood

The most underrated city in Africa 🇩🇿 Oran is the second largest city in Algeria, known for its Mediterranean coastline, beautiful architecture, vibrant cafe culture, incredible food, and raï music.
